headline: Approved Pattie DeMaria as interim Westbrook Middle School principal and 10 other staff nominations.
summary: Enrollment is 2,377, 25 more than last year. The district hired 54 new employees and is starting a review of special education with Great Schools. A parent asked for exceptions to the joint-custody bus stop rule, and several drivers and staff opposed them.
decisions: Approved 11 staff nominations, including interim Westbrook Middle School principal Pattie DeMaria, 6-0.

### 14. Public Participation (any school related matter; 3 minutes per speaker; one time only)

Chair Andrea Mancuso read a letter from David Morse into the record. The letter was in praise of Transportation Director Melissa Foye and the Transportation Department. (letter included in the minutes)

Chair Andrea Mancuso stated that there were not be any debate or discussion on this issue during public comment. Chair Andrea Mancuso announced that the matter would receive another public-comment opportunity at the September 23 Policy Committee meeting at 5:00 PM, where the committee could consider whether to further discuss Policy EEA, Student Transportation.

Kristen Harvey (177 Mast Road) spoke against the district's policy allowing children from joint-custody families to use only one designated bus stop/address, even when both parents' homes are legal residences within the district. She argued that her children had successfully used two addresses since 2022 and asked the district to create a joint-custody transportation variance for families able to provide fixed, predictable schedules.

Several bus drivers and transportation staff strongly opposed making exceptions to the policy. Their central arguments were:

- The transportation department is severely understaffed, with one driver stating staffing had fallen from 28 full-time drivers to 14.
- Multiple bus stops or changing schedules make it much harder for drivers and teachers to know where each student is supposed to be, increasing the risk of students being misplaced or unaccounted for.
- Drivers described situations in which students could get off at an unexpected stop, potentially triggering searches involving transportation staff and law enforcement.
- Staff argued that making exceptions for one family could create a precedent and a flood of similar requests, making an already difficult system even harder to manage.
- Drivers emphasized that consistent routes and designated stops are important for student safety, accountability, and substitute drivers' ability to know which students should be on the bus.
